item.title: Cannobio, barracks named after Angelo Spagnulo
item.description: At Cannobio the Carabinieri Station remembers the chosen carabiniere killed in 2005 at the age of 25 while trying to stop a robbery.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Cannobio dedicated the barracks to Angelo Spagnulo - Spagnulo was killed at 25 during a robbery - The ceremony took place on September 24
## Key facts - What → dedication of the Carabinieri Station barracks - Where → Cannobio - To whom → Carabiniere Scelto Angelo Spagnulo - When → September 24 - Killing → 2005, at 25, in the province of Taranto
On September 24, Cannobio dedicated the Carabinieri Station barracks to Carabiniere Scelto Angelo Spagnulo, who was remembered during a brief but heartfelt ceremony. The choice links the city outpost to the memory of a member of the Carabinieri Corps who was killed at 25, in 2005, while trying to stop a robbery.
Spagnulo was off duty and was in the province of Taranto. During an attempted robbery, he placed himself between a robber and a young woman. A shotgun blast killed him. He also had a broken leg and was unarmed: the sense of duty, recalled during the ceremony, was stronger than the conditions in which he found himself. The act is thus associated with an intervention carried out despite being in a situation of great difficulty.
Twenty years have passed, but the pain has remained, together with the profound dignity of the family members. In Cannobio were his mother Nunzia, his sister Camilla and his brothers Alessandro and Francesco. Their presence accompanied the remembrance of the Carabiniere Scelto and gave the brief ceremony the face of the family.
### The act remembered during the ceremony
With the dedication, Spagnulo's name is now linked to the Carabinieri Station in Cannobio. The ceremony did not only commemorate the death in 2005, but also the choice made by a young carabiniere who, while off duty, intervened during a robbery.
The reference to Cannobio is concrete: the dedicated barracks is that of the Carabinieri Station, while the 2005 incident occurred in the province of Taranto. Spagnulo's memory was entrusted to a Carabinieri facility where his name is linked to the daily work of the service members. The dedication brings together the personal memory of the man and the significance of his act. In the account of the ceremony, Spagnulo was unarmed, had a broken leg and nevertheless tried to place himself between the robber and the young woman. The bond between Angelo Spagnulo and Cannobio also goes back to the months spent in the city before the transfer to the Provincial Command of Verbania. His memory is still alive in the place where he spent that period and where the current commander of the Station, Giuseppe Rossini, knew him personally. Rossini strongly wanted the dedication ceremony.
Mayor Gianmaria Minazzi did the honors, together with his fellow mayors of the area. In his speech, Minazzi indicated the Cannobio station as a fundamental garrison. He linked the dedication to the responsibility of not forgetting those who served the State to the ultimate sacrifice, explaining that Spagnulo's name recalls the highest values ​​of the State.
### The meaning for Cannobio
The mayor also presented the dedication as a source of pride for Cannobio. Linking the name of the municipality to that of a man who dedicated his life to the highest values ​​of the State, according to Minazzi, means leaving a call for solidarity. The ceremony combined the function of the barracks and the memory of a sacrifice made during an attempted robbery.
The presence of family members accompanied the memory on the day of the dedication. Mother Nunzia, Camilla, Alessandro and Francesco participated in a moment described as short but heartfelt, together with the institutional representatives present. The pain, after twenty years, was indicated as still present, despite a profound dignity.
The subsequent transfer to the Provincial Command of Verbania has been recalled as part of Spagnulo's history. The Cannobio station has chosen to link its name to that of the chosen carabiniere, keeping at the center the sense of duty that led him to intervene despite being free from duty, wounded in the leg and unarmed. The value of the dedication arises from the facts remembered during the ceremony and from the personal relationship that Spagnulo had with the commander Giuseppe Rossini. The name on the barracks now enters the work of the force through the daily life of the Carabinieri station. The provincial commander, Colonel Loris Baldassarre, recalled that those who give their lives for others are alive forever and stated that Spagnulo is present today together with the military. In his reading, the department named after the hero of the force must represent a constant stimulus for all the carabinieri who work there.
Baldassarre also recalled the role of the Carabinieri Station as a fundamental garrison and place for a community to listen to on a daily basis. The reference concerns the work carried out every day within it. Spagnulo's memory is thus connected to the task of the military and to the daily listening of the community, according to the message entrusted to the ceremony.
### The message from the Carabinieri leaders
General Andrea Paterna, commander of the Piedmont and Valle d'Aosta Carabinieri Legion, also spoke at the ceremony. Paterna described the job of a policeman as exhilarating, but often ruthless. His speech recalled the responsibility of those who work today in a barracks that bears the name of Spagnulo.
> «The only real way to honor Angelo Spagnulo is to make him feel proud of having given his name to a barracks where carabinieri animated by his same courage work. It is a daily model to follow, to close the circle that it has opened, to make this world a better place."
Paterna's message links the dedication to an everyday example. The model to follow is that of carabinieri animated by the same courage as Spagnulo, with the objective indicated by the general of closing the circle opened by his gesture and making the world a better place. For the Cannobio Station, the name thus becomes a constant reminder of the sense of duty and courage remembered during the ceremony, for the soldiers who work there.

item.title: Ticino kindergarten: transition from AOZ to ORs raises employment concerns
item.description: From January AOZ leaves the centres of Balerna and Chiasso; ORS could hire up to 80 of the 120 employees, according to the unions – 40 positions at risk.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - From January, AOZ will leave the asylum seeker centers in Ticino - ORS might hire no more than 80 of the 120 employees - Unions estimate 40 fewer jobs - SEM: 60% quality, 40% price in ORS selection
- Change: AOZ replaced by ORS - Locations: Pasture in Balerna and Via Motta in Chiasso - AOZ staff: 120 employees - Union estimate: no more than 80 hires - SEM criteria: 60% quality, 40% price
From January, in the federal asylum seeker centers in Ticino, assistance services will transition from AOZ to ORS. The change was decided at a national level by the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM), and in Ticino, the news is accompanied by VPOD's concern for employment and working conditions.
AOZ, the Zurich Asylum Organization, is an entity linked to the City on the Limmat. ORS, Organization for Refugee Services, is a private company belonging to a British multinational. The two acronyms therefore indicate providers with different structures and profiles, not just a change of name.
Today, AOZ employs 120 people in Ticino. The staff operates between the Pasture center in Balerna and the Via Motta center in Chiasso, which is currently closed due to a temporary decrease in migratory flows. According to union estimates, ORS would be ready to hire no more than 80 people. The hypothetical difference is 40 job positions.
Edoardo Cappelletti, co-secretary of VPOD Ticino, links the employment risk to ORS's willingness not to reabsorb the entire workforce. In his opinion, the transition could also affect the collective labor agreement (CCL): AOZ applies one based on that of the City of Zurich staff, while ORS would not be willing to take over the current agreement. For the union, the guarantees offered would not be equivalent.
The Confederation's position is different. Contacted by RSI, SEM guaranteed that 'the change of service provider does not entail any reduction of personnel.' It also explained that the choice of ORS was evaluated 60% on quality and 40% on price.
The discussion has also moved to the institutional level. A staff assembly met in Balerna with the unions to define their demands. The central request is to maintain current employment and entrust SEM with the supervision of the handover. Cappelletti also called upon the Ticino Government and the Parliamentary Delegation. For those following professional opportunities in the region, the editorial reference remains the job announcements page, separate from official communications on the service provider change. ...

The source does not indicate forms, individual deadlines, or documents to be submitted. The concrete actions that can be derived are therefore those already defined by the staff and unions, along with the requests addressed to the institutions. A more detailed path would not be supported by the original text.
### 1. Identifying the Scope
The change concerns the assistance service in federal asylum seeker centers in Ticino. For the staff, the reference points are the Pasture center in Balerna and the Via Motta center in Chiasso, which the source describes as temporarily closed due to a decrease in migration flows. This allows distinguishing the site affected by the mandate from the current operational situation of the individual center.
### 2. Following the Union Negotiations
The staff assembly met in Balerna with the unions on Friday afternoon to define their demands. The key point to follow is the maintenance of employment as it is today. Alongside the number of employees, the fate of the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) must be observed: AOZ applies a contract based on that of the City of Zurich staff, while VPOD reports that ORS would not be willing to adopt it.
### 3. Requesting Oversight of the Transition
The union's stated request is for the SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) to supervise the handover to guarantee employment. In the same discussion, the Ticino Government and the Cantonal Parliament Delegation were called upon. These are, according to the source, the institutional bodies to be involved; no other offices or procedures are indicated.
### 4. Keeping Available Timelines Separate
The text indicates the change of operator from January and the arrival of Gaby Szöllösy as head of ORS operations from October 1st. It does not provide the exact day of the handover in the centers nor a deadline for individual positions. The designated director was the general secretary of the Conference of Cantonal Directors of Social Works and, previously, headed communications at SEM, the same federal office that currently awards mandates.

item.title: Thirty travelers in Gallarate after the train to Malpensa
item.description: About thirty travelers were stranded at Gallarate station on the evening of 22 September, waiting for train 2989 at 23.24, which was replaced by buses due to nighttime works.
item.content:encoded:
.... The case compares the scheduled service with what the traveler sees on site. Before September 22, the change was communicated through notices and the timetable search engine: 2989 would not run between Gallarate and Saronno, and the route would be covered by buses as far as Saronno. On the night of September 22, however, the systems update had removed that change. The result was an operational contradiction: the commercial service had been organized differently, while the station continued to display the train.
For anyone who needs to continue their journey in the evening or reach the airport, the difference is not merely formal. The presence of the train, the lights being on, and the announcements had created an indication that was coherent only on the surface. The timetable search engine, also consulted by customer service at least initially, returned 2989 as an active service. Under these conditions, the passenger was not faced with simply incomplete information, but with indications that contradicted one another.
### The infrastructure issue
The explanation provided by Trenord refers to the structure of the line. Gallarate is on the Rfi network. The connection toward Malpensa and Saronno, however, involves the Ferrovienord network up to Milano Bovisa, then the route returns to Rfi tracks up to Milano Centrale. The works referred to in the notices concerned the Saronno-Castellanza section of the Ferrovienord network.
According to the company, the update of September 21 was the responsibility of the infrastructure managers and had caused the change to disappear. The reconstruction was carried out with Rfi and FerrovieNord, identified as responsible for the Malpensa-Bovisa section. This explains why a cancellation scheduled days in advance remained correctly shown in the original notices, but not in the systems used that evening.
To read the case in practical terms, it is useful to separate three moments: the decision to carry out the works, the publication of the bus replacement service and the updating of information in the station. The first and second had been prepared; the third erased the decisive piece of data. For those traveling between the stations concerned, the risk arises precisely when these three sources do not coincide. The reference to mezzi pubblici Ticino may help compare transport options, but it does not replace the specific notices concerning the line described.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ### How to navigate during the works period
Those departing from Gallarate on weekday nights between 14 September and 30 October can follow the sequence indicated by the official notices:
1. Check whether the journey concerns one of services 2985, 2987 or 2989. The change concerned the Gallarate-Saronno route, with replacement buses. 2. For 2989, check the scheduled departure at 23.24 from Gallarate and the bus destination as far as Saronno. Trenord also reported an additional special bus service departing at the same time, bound for Malpensa. 3. Compare the Rfi or Trenord notice with what appears on the timetable search engine and on the boards. On 22 September, these channels did not show the same information: the check is therefore needed to identify any discrepancies. 4. If the train still appears but the doors remain closed, ask staff for information when available and contact Trenord customer service. On the evening described, customer service also initially saw 2989 as operating. 5. If the station is closed and there are no staff members, the source documents that some travelers, after midnight, made their own arrangements. One group called a car with a driver and reached Malpensa at around 2. The source describes this as passengers organizing independently and, separately, reports the special bus service arranged by Trenord.
### What changes after the verification
Trenord communicated that, once the anomaly was identified, the infrastructure manager modified the station announcements. The company therefore indicated that the problem should not recur. The same note specified that the special bus service had been arranged, even though that evening it was not signaled on site.
The point to retain, for those who need to organize a journey, is the distinction between the bus to Saronno and the additional service bound for Malpensa: these are two indications reported in Trenord's account and should be read together with the departure point, Gallarate, and the time of 23.24. To compare the cost of a road-based option, costo auto pendolare is available. To complete the planning of work-related expenses, also use calcolatore stipendio.

item.description: Lombardy Region allocates over 1,5 million to Gravedona ed Uniti and Porlezza: 502.082 euros to the Chiesa della Madonna della Soledad and 1 million to Villa Marzorati.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- Over 1.5 million destined for two municipalities - €502,082 for the Church of Madonna della Soledad - €1 million for Villa Marzorati - Integrated Culture Projects Call 2026-2029
## Key facts
- Municipalities → Gravedona ed Uniti and Porlezza - Total amount → over €1.5 million - Gravedona ed Uniti → €502,082 - Work → Church of Madonna della Soledad - Porlezza → €1 million - Work → Villa Marzorati - Call → Integrated Culture Projects 2026-2029 - Subjects → Lombardy Region and Fondazione Cariplo
### Two precise destinations
Gravedona ed Uniti and Porlezza are the two municipalities receiving a cultural investment announced through the ranking just published of the Integrated Culture Projects Call 2026-2029. The initiative is carried out by Lombardy Region in collaboration with Fondazione Cariplo and allocates a total of over €1.5 million to the two territories.
In Gravedona ed Uniti, €502,082 are allocated. The sum will be used for the restoration and enhancement of the Church of Madonna della Soledad, indicated as a historical and cultural asset of particular value. In Porlezza, €1 million is assigned for the recovery of Villa Marzorati.
Commenting on the ranking is Gigliola Spelzini, regional councillor of Alto Lago. In her comment, Spelzini presents the two interventions as an investment in the places of local history and their usability. The allocation of resources therefore follows two precise lines: intervene on the church of Gravedona ed Uniti with restoration and enhancement, and recover the villa of Porlezza.
The funding concerns two different places, but is described as coordinated support for the culture of the two municipalities. For the councillor, the value of the operation is concrete because it allows the recovery of important places of the territory's history and makes them increasingly usable. ## Benefits for the local area
### What it means for communities
Spelzini's statements attribute tangible value to the two projects for local communities. The reason given is the restoration of places important to the area's history, along with the possibility of making them increasingly accessible. The perspective therefore concerns the preservation of heritage assets and their cultural enhancement, according to the terms used in the comment on the ranking.
For Gravedona ed Uniti, the project concerns a historical and cultural asset of particular value. For Porlezza, the restoration of Villa Marzorati is associated with strengthening and enhancing the area's cultural offering. The two projects are thus described with specific objectives, but within the same focus on local heritage.
> «Regione Lombardia demonstrates once again its attention to municipalities and the enhancement of local heritage».
Spelzini links this attention to the broader role attributed to investment in culture. Preserving identity is one of the stated aims, together with creating new spaces and opportunities for citizens, associations and visitors. Existing heritage is considered a living resource, capable of generating new opportunities for local communities.
The councillor's reaction therefore highlights the territorial dimension of the operation: the places receiving funding will have to be restored, enhanced and made increasingly accessible, contributing to the cultural offering of the municipalities involved. ## From preservation to opportunities
### The expected outcome for the two properties
The stated outlook for the two grants concerns how the restored properties can be made available to the local area. In Gravedona ed Uniti, the restoration and enhancement of the Church of Madonna della Soledad are linked to the recovery of a particularly valuable historical and cultural asset. In Porlezza, the recovery of Villa Marzorati is presented as the intervention that will make it possible to consolidate and enhance the area’s cultural offering.
The aim identified by Spelzini is to make these places increasingly accessible. Culture is described as a tool for preserving identity, but also for creating new spaces and opportunities. The recipients mentioned in the statement are citizens, associations and visitors.
The endpoint announced by the councillor is the transformation of existing heritage into a living resource, capable of generating new opportunities for local communities. This is the follow-up that the source associates with the publication of the ranking: the funds allocated to the two municipalities are linked to the possibility of making important places in local history newly accessible and supporting the cultural offering.
For Gravedona ed Uniti and Porlezza, the investment is therefore presented as an intervention in the heritage and, at the same time, as an opportunity for the communities. The commentary focuses on the cultural and community value of the two projects, carried out as part of the Progetti Integrati della Cultura 2026-2029 call with the collaboration between Regione Lombardia and Fondazione Cariplo.

Shortly after midnight, in Como, patrol units from the State Police responded to Via Zezio following a report received by the Operations Center. A caller reported that two people were searching through a parked car after smashing its windows.
The officers identified two individuals matching the descriptions they had received. When they saw the patrol car, the two tried to leave quickly, but they were stopped. The search led to the discovery of a window-breaking hammer, several credit cards, banknotes, Swiss francs and documents.
The check was then extended to the streets adjacent to the location of the report. On Via Ferrari and Via Santo Garovaglio, the patrol cars spotted five more vehicles with their windows smashed. The inspection therefore covered the car reported on Via Zezio and the additional vehicles damaged on the two nearby streets. The check thus included the location of the initial report and the two adjacent streets patrolled by the units.
The two men, a 30-year-old Moroccan and a 23-year-old Spanish national with previous police records, are both in Italy without a fixed address. The operation concluded with their arrest for aggravated theft as accomplices and an investigation into aggravated criminal damage. The operational sequence begins with the report received by the local Operations Control Room and the dispatch of the patrol crews toward Via Zezio. At that point, a car parked with its windows smashed had been reported. The caller did not limit themselves to reporting the damage: they also provided a description of the two individuals.
As they drove along the street, the officers saw two people matching that description. When the two noticed the patrol car, they tried to move away quickly. Once stopped, they proved hostile to the check. The Police carried out a more thorough inspection, which led to the discovery of a glass-breaking hammer along with credit cards, banknotes, Swiss francs and documents.
The next part of the intervention concerned checks of the nearby streets. The crews drove along several adjacent roads to determine whether other vehicles had been damaged. The check focused in particular on Via Ferrari and Via Santo Garovaglio. On these two streets, another five vehicles with their window glass smashed were observed.
The check of the adjacent streets therefore added the identification of five additional damaged vehicles to the initial report. The operational sequence starts from the car on Via Zezio and continues with the check of Via Ferrari and Via Santo Garovaglio, the streets traveled by the patrol cars after the first report. Taken to police headquarters, the two were fully identified. The identification revealed that the 23-year-old Spaniard had some police records for the same offenses. This information emerged during the identification at police headquarters.
The characterization communicated by the State Police distinguishes between the two aspects indicated in the operation. Both were arrested for aggravated theft committed jointly. As for aggravated damage, they are instead under investigation.
This wording distinguishes the arrest for theft from the investigation into aggravated damage, although it refers to the same intervention by the Flying Squad. After the identification and the formalities carried out at police headquarters, both were placed at the disposal of the Judicial Authority. The subsequent direct trial hearing was scheduled for this morning.
The immediate follow-up to the operation is therefore linked to the judicial step already indicated. The next step for both is the direct trial hearing scheduled for this morning. The proceeding concerns both arrestees, while the reference to previous records for the same offenses concerns the 23-year-old identified at police headquarters.
The procedure described maintains the distinction between the two outcomes: arrest for aggravated theft committed jointly and investigation for aggravated damage. The arrestees were therefore placed at the disposal of the Judicial Authority for the subsequent direct trial hearing scheduled for this morning.

item.title: Reported for dumping waste in Lake Maggiore in Brezzo di Bedero
item.description: Forest Carabinieri report owner: rubble from the terrace thrown into water at a depth of 7-13 meters.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Construction debris in Lake Maggiore at Brezzo di Bedero - Property owner reported - Divers working between 7 and 13 metres - Recovery and restoration at the owner's expense
## Key facts - Location → Brezzo di Bedero, Lake Maggiore - Authority → Forest Carabinieri of the Luino Unit - Alleged offence → abandonment of non-hazardous waste - Materials → concrete conglomerates and tiles - Lakebed → between 7 and 13 metres deep - Obligation → recovery at their own expense and restoration of the site
### The report in Brezzo di Bedero
It was in Brezzo di Bedero, near Lake Maggiore, that the Forest Carabinieri of the Luino Unit reported the owner of a property to the Judicial Authority. The alleged offence is abandonment of non-hazardous waste.
According to the officers' investigations, the construction waste produced by renovating the house's terrace apparently ended up directly in the lake waters. The allegation therefore arose from the presence in the water of material from work carried out on the property.
The investigation was triggered by a report from a resident. The man had noticed some people throwing material from the construction site into the water and, after filing a formal complaint, brought the case to the attention of the forest carabinieri. The officers went to the site and found several piles of demolition material in the lake.
The debris identified included mainly concrete conglomerates and tiles. The account reported by the carabinieri links these materials to the renovation of the terrace and their subsequent discharge into the lake. The property owner is the person reported at the end of the investigation, while the incident is described as an alleged abandonment of non-hazardous waste.
The initial investigation thus led from the resident's report to direct verification of the presence of the piles. The incident concerns a spot in Lake Maggiore at Brezzo di Bedero and a construction project whose waste, according to the carabinieri, was abandoned in the water. The case was reconstructed through the report and the discovery in the lake of the piles linked to the terrace work, elements underlying the forest officers' intervention and the report to the Judicial Authority. ## The Lakebed Inspection
### Inspection from the Lake
To determine how much material had been dumped and assess the environmental damage, an inspection of the lakebed was ordered. Checks were also carried out from the lake, using the patrol boat of the Compagnia Carabinieri di Luino and with the support of divers from the Associazione Nazionale Istruttori Subacquei.
The dives made it possible to identify and film a large quantity of debris lying on the bottom at a depth of between 7 and 13 meters. The presence of the material beneath the surface was therefore documented during the underwater activities, along with the depth at which the debris had been deposited.
The inspection was ordered to quantify the dumped material and assess the environmental damage. The activities from the lake involved the patrol boat of the Compagnia Carabinieri di Luino and the association's divers, who worked to identify and film what was on the lakebed.
According to the reconstruction by the Carabinieri, the material is believed to have been dumped deliberately. Investigators hypothesize that the aim was to avoid the costs of transporting and disposing of it at authorized facilities, thereby obtaining an unlawful financial advantage. This reconstruction was formulated at the end of the investigations into the material originating from the construction site and its presence in the waters of Lake Maggiore.
The forest Carabinieri also emphasize the decisive role played by the report received from the local area. The resident noticed some people throwing construction waste into the water and filed a formal complaint, enabling the checks to begin. For the forest Carabinieri, cooperation between citizens and law enforcement is an essential tool for combating environmental violations and protecting the area. In the case of Brezzo di Bedero, the report led to the inspection of the lakebed and the documentation of the debris through the dives. ## The follow-up to the investigation
### Recovery and restoration
At the end of the investigations, a report was filed against the property owner. The report comes after checks on the piles of demolition material and after the inspection that located and filmed the debris on the lakebed.
For the sole uncontrolled discharge of waste into the water by a business owner, the law provides for imprisonment from six months to two years or a fine of 3,000 to 27,000 euros. This provision is cited together with the charge indicated by the carabinieri and concerns the discharge of waste into the water.
The carabinieri do not rule out, however, that other criminal offenses may also apply, given the special environmental and landscape protection afforded to the basin of Lake Maggiore. The report is therefore accompanied by the possibility that further aspects relating to the protection of the basin and the places concerned may be assessed.
The man will also be required to recover, at his own expense, the material that ended up on the lakebed and to completely restore the condition of the site. The obligation concerns the removal of the debris located during the dives and the restoration of the area affected by the spill.
The follow-up indicated by the investigations therefore includes the recovery of the material and the complete restoration of the condition of the site, in addition to the assessment of the other criminal offenses that the carabinieri do not rule out. The operations will have to concern the material deposited in the lake and the effects of the dumping of waste produced by the renovation of the terrace.
The case of Brezzo di Bedero thus remains linked both to the report against the owner and to the intervention required on the lakebed. The material will have to be recovered at the man's expense, while the basin of Lake Maggiore will have to be completely restored to the condition it was in before the spill.

item.description: The Court of Assizes of Varese sentenced Marco Manfrinati to life imprisonment for the murder of Fabio Limido and the attempted murder of Lavinia Limido.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Manfrinati was sentenced to life imprisonment - The ruling is a first-instance judgment - Fabio Limido was killed in Casbeno - Lavinia Limido was seriously injured
## Key facts - Defendant → Marco Manfrinati - Court → Varese Assize Court - Judgment → life imprisonment and daytime isolation - Location → via Ciro Menotti, Casbeno, Varese - Date of events → 6 May 2024 - Victim → Fabio Limido, 71 years old - Injured person → Lavinia Limido - Defense attorney → Elio Giannangeli
### The decision Marco Manfrinati was sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Fabio Limido and the attempted murder of his former wife, Lavinia Limido. The ruling came at the end of this morning and was handed down by the Varese Assize Court. For the former lawyer from Busto Arsizio, this is a first-instance judgment, issued in the proceedings concerning the events on via Ciro Menotti, in the Casbeno district.
The legal case concerns the attack of 6 May 2024. On that day, Limido, 71, intervened to defend his daughter, who was attacked by her former husband in the middle of the street and in front of her workplace. Fabio Limido was stabbed to death. Lavinia Limido was struck in the face and neck and was seriously injured; she was rushed to hospital in desperate circumstances.
The Varese judges also ordered daytime isolation for Manfrinati. The defendant, represented by attorney Elio Giannangeli, was not in court today. The report on the judgment brings together the two events for which Manfrinati had been imprisoned: the murder of his former father-in-law, Fabio Limido, and the attempted murder of his former wife, the victim's daughter. The location remains identified as via Ciro Menotti, in the Casbeno district of Varese, where the attack took place and where police and emergency services later intervened.
The report therefore identifies two distinct outcomes of the same attack: the death of Fabio Limido and the serious injuries suffered by Lavinia Limido. These are the events connected to the legal case heard today before the Varese Assize Court. ## The reconstruction on Via Menotti
### The sequence on the street The focal point of the incident is Via Ciro Menotti, in the Casbeno district of Varese. The scene unfolded in the street, in front of Lavinia Limido’s workplace. According to the reconstruction reported by the source, Manfrinati’s ex-wife had been attacked by her ex-husband. Her father, Fabio Limido, 71, intervened to defend her.

Lavinia, meanwhile, was wounded in the face and neck and was left seriously injured. She was then rushed desperately to hospital in an attempt to save her.
The police and emergency services arrived on Via Menotti, as also documented by the scene on 6 May 2024. The next stage was Manfrinati’s arrest: the former lawyer from Busto was detained by the police in front of Marta Criscuolo, Fabio Limido’s wife.
The account of the events therefore links the same place to the various moments of the incident: the attack in the street, the intervention of the 71-year-old, the stabbings, the emergency response for Lavinia and the detention of the defendant. The source places all these stages in the Casbeno district and identifies the family relationships indicated in the incident: Manfrinati was Lavinia’s ex-husband, while Fabio Limido was her former father-in-law.
Via Ciro Menotti is therefore the common reference point for the most concrete part of the reconstruction: the attack took place here, the police and emergency services converged here and the police detained Manfrinati here. The source links that place to the relationships between the people involved, without separating the scene from their family relationships. ## The procedural framework
### The elements of the sentence The sentence delivered today in Varese is described as a first-instance decision. The Court of Assizes of the provincial capital ruled at the end of the late morning on the proceedings involving the defendant Marco Manfrinati, the former Busto Arsizio lawyer imprisoned for the murder of Fabio Limido and the attempted murder of Lavinia Limido.
For Manfrinati, the reports highlight two elements of the decision: the life sentence and the daytime isolation ordered by the Varese judges. Daytime isolation is indicated as an additional provision relative to the sentence. The ruling therefore concerns the two events for which the former Busto Arsizio lawyer was in prison: the death of his former father-in-law and the assault on his former wife, the victim's daughter.
Manfrinati was not present in the courtroom today. His defense is entrusted to lawyer Elio Giannangeli, mentioned in the reports alongside the news of the sentence. The decision was made public following the events of May 6, 2024, when police arrested Manfrinati in via Ciro Menotti, in Casbeno, while Lavinia Limido was being rescued and Fabio Limido had already been killed.
The day's reports conclude with the ruling of the Varese judges and the classification of the sentence as first-instance. The name of the victim and the name of the injured person remain separate in the formulation of the news: Fabio Limido is linked to the murder, Lavinia Limido to the attempted murder. The source reports the decision through these elements: the level of judgment, the penalty, the daytime isolation, the defense, and the absence of the defendant in court.

item.title: Pay equity in Ticino's public sector: next steps
item.description: Over thirty municipalities in Ticino have joined the Charter for equal pay; in 2024 the difference in the public sector was 847 francs and Locarno invests over 3.2 million a year in work-family reconciliation measures.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - More than thirty Ticino municipalities have signed up to the Charter - In 2024 the difference in the public sector was 847 francs - Locarno spends over 3.2 million a year on work-family reconciliation
## Key facts - Principle: equal pay for work of equal value - Charter: five articles, initiated by the Federal Council in 2016 - Ticino signature: Manuele Bertoli, then president of the Government - Swiss signatories: 175 among cantons, municipalities, consortia and para-state companies - Locarno: 423 employees, more than half women - Municipal nursery: approximately 80 places - Investment in Locarno: 199 francs per capita - Expenditure in the district: approximately 4.2 million francs a year
The Charter for pay equality in the public sector bears the signature of Manuele Bertoli for the Canton of Ticino, then president of the Ticino Government. Initiated by the Federal Council in 2016, it is turning ten and consists of five articles built around a constitutional principle: the right to equal pay for work of equal value.
In Ticino, more than thirty municipalities signed up following the request of the Council of State. Rachele Santoro, Ticino's delegate for equal opportunities, expressed surprise at the number of signatories.
> “We were nevertheless surprised that more than thirty municipalities signed up to this Charter and to the Council of State's request to sign it,” Rachele Santoro, Ticino's delegate for equal opportunities, told Quotidiano.
### Signing does not conclude the process
The next step, according to Santoro, is to understand how to implement the commitments made. The first check concerns the individual bodies' pay practices and the guarantee of equality between men and women. The sign-up is therefore not presented as a final declaration, but as the start of an internal review.
The issue stems from a precise figure: in 2024, there was still a difference of 847 francs in Ticino's public sector. The source makes clear that it is not enough to declare salary classes and pay applicable to everyone. The disparity may result from discrimination in pay, but also from working conditions that do not guarantee equal access to management positions and career advancement.
In Switzerland, the Charter has been signed by 175 entities, including cantons, municipalities, consortia and para-state companies. Within the framework described, their task is to set a good example not only in terms of pay.
Locarno is among the signatories. Mayor Nicola Pini explained that the City had strengthened work-family compatibility through leave, flexibility, part-time work and job sharing. Locarno has 423 employees, more than half of them women, and calculated an investment of 199 francs per capita for this item. Among the measures mentioned is the municipal asilo nido, with approximately 80 places.
In the district, the study on merging with the other municipalities indicated that approximately 60% of nursery places are concentrated in Locarno. The final certainty remains that expressed by the source: in Switzerland and Ticino, people are still talking about disparities, not pay equality. ### From signature to practice
The difference between a signature and a salary policy is seen in the step indicated by the Charter: analysing what the entities actually do. A formally equal salary class for all does not, by itself, exclude a different result if access conditions to managerial roles or career paths change. This is the reason why the source broadens the control from the payslip to the organisation of work.
| Area | Practical reading of the source | |---|---| | Remuneration | checking salary practices and any possible discrimination on the payslip | | Career | verifying access to managerial functions and career progression | | Work‑life balance | considering leave, flexibility, part‑time and job sharing |
For a cross‑border worker employed in a participating municipality, the comparison is therefore not limited to the amount received: it also concerns the conditions under which one can access responsibilities and build a career. It is a key of interpretation linked to work in the Canton of Ticino, not an individual measure described by the source.
Locarno shows how reconcilability can be translated into resources and services. The 199 francs per capita calculated by the City and the expenditure of over 3.2 million francs on the roughly 4.2 million francs invested each year in the catchment area give a concrete dimension of the commitment. The data on nursery places, with about 60% concentrated in Locarno, adds a territorial dimension to the discussion.
The cross‑border reader must also know where this news ends: the source does not mention the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, reimbursements, withholding tax or double taxation. The text remains focused on work and equality in the public sector of the Canton of Ticino. Those who wish to accompany the reading with a numerical check can use the payslip simulator, without confusing it with an analysis of career and work‑life balance practices.

item.title: Ambrì beat Lugano 5-3 in the first derby of the season
item.description: Ambrì conquers the Cornèr Arena with a 5-3 score decided in the second period. The blue-and-whites rise to 11 points, while Lugano remains last with 5 points.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Ambrì beats Lugano 5-3 at Cornèr Arena. - The derby is decided by three goals in the middle period. - The blue-and-whites remain second with 11 points in 6 games. - Lugano is last with 5 points in 4 games.
## Key facts - Result: Lugano-Ambrì 3-5 - Venue: Cornèr Arena - Date: 26 September 2026 - Period scores: 2-2, 1-3, 0-0 - Attendance: 6'733 - Ambrì: 11 points in 6 games - Lugano: 5 points in 4 games - Referees: Kaukokari, Lemelin, Stalder, Urfer
On 26 September 2026, the first derby of the season went to Ambrì, who managed to conquer Lugano's Cornèr Arena with a score of 5-3. The blue-and-whites built their success on a performance marked by heart, determination and above all discipline, at the end of an entertaining match full of changes in momentum.
Lugano, on the other hand, ended the evening with a negative balance. The black-and-white team was described as lacking clarity and being too imprecise, especially when Ambrì found space to strike. The result also confirmed the different directions taken by the two teams in this early stage of the season.
### The opening minutes
The home team took the lead after just one minute and 56 seconds. Alessio Bertaggia capitalized on a defensive error by HCAP and put Lugano 1-0 up, immediately giving the derby the expected pace.
Ambrì's response came just over a minute later, on the power play. At 3'16'' Järventie equalized in the power play, finding an angle deemed impossible. For the forward, it was his fourth goal in two games and his fifth in the last three games mentioned in the report.
At 7'31'' Lugano moved ahead again. Thürkauf turned a great pass from Shore in the slot into a goal, with Alatalo listed in the play-by-play for the 5-on-4. Ambrì, however, continued to stay in the game and found the evening's second equalizer at 18'15''.
The 2-2 goal was scored by Tommaso De Luca with an angled wrist shot, again during a power play. In the first period, the two teams therefore scored twice each, leaving the contest open and setting up the subsequent change in the match's pace. The middle period shifted the balance of the derby in Ambrì's favor. In the first part of the period, it was the blue-and-whites who created the best chances, particularly through Järventie and Borradori. Lugano nevertheless managed to strike first, capitalizing on Shore's airborne deflection of a shot by Zanetti.
The new black-and-white lead lasted just 37 seconds. Borradori scored the third equalizer of the evening thanks to an incisive, perfectly timed pass from Heed, bringing the score back to 3-3. The exchange of goals thus prolonged the series of swings that had characterized the derby from the outset.
### The decisive goals
Between 35' and 37' Ambrì scored twice. At 34'55'' Joly made it 4-3 after a move set up by Kodytek. At 36'44'' the fifth goal also arrived, with Lukas Landry firing the puck past Schlegel at the end of a fine combination with his brother Manix Landry.
The Leventina side's lead was considered deserved based on what was seen in the middle period. In that period, Lugano showed up very little in front of Wüthrich, while Ambrì took advantage of the Under-Ceneri side's excessive defensive looseness to pull away for good.
In the third period, Mitell's team tried to close the gap. Lugano attempted to make use of the greater freshness of its players, but Heed and his teammates defended with great discipline. Ambrì thus completed its mission without conceding any further goals: the final period score was in fact 0-0.
The victory adds to the Leventina side's excellent start to the season, as they did not pay the price for the fatigue of the match played the previous day against the Lions. Lugano, on the other hand, had rested on Friday, but continued its inconsistent form at the start of the championship.
With the three points won at the Cornèr Arena, Ambrì defended second place and reached 11 points in 6 matches. Lugano remained at the bottom of the standings with 5 points in 4 games, despite having played two fewer matches than Kloten and Langnau. The match report sets the final result at 3-5, with partial scores of 2-2, 1-3, and 0-0. There were 6,733 spectators present at the Cornèr Arena. The listed referees are Kaukokari and Lemelin, with Stalder and Urfer completing the officiating crew reported in the scoresheet.
### The team scoresheet
For Lugano, the report lists Schlegel; M. Müller and Thomson; B. Zanetti and Aebischer; J. Peltonen and Alatalo; Canonica, Sanford and Fazzini; Olsson, Thürkauf and Kupari; Lycksell, Shore and Innala; Bertaggia, Tanner and M. Zanetti. Among the black-and-white players mentioned during the match are the scorers Bertaggia, Thürkauf and Shore, as well as the men involved in the decisive actions of the first and second periods.
The Ambrì lineup included Wüthrich; Worge and Heed; Pezzullo and D. Wüthrich; I. Dotti and Z. Dotti; Häfliger; Järventie, Schnarr and De Luca; Müller, Kodytek and Joly; Borradori, Heim and Muggli; L. Landry, M. Landry, Bosson and Kostner. The scoresheet thus brings together the players who participated in the white-and-blue victory, including Järventie, De Luca, Borradori, Joly and the Landry brothers, who scored the goals for Ambrì.
In the other matches of the evening, Zurich achieved its sixth full seasonal success in six matches played, beating Kloten 3-2 in the derby. Rappi earned two points in Porrentruy, prevailing 5-4 in overtime.
Davos defeated Lausanne with a score of 4-2. Fribourg, on the other hand, overcame Langnau in overtime, closing the challenge at 4-3. These are the other results reported alongside the Cornèr Arena derby as part of the championship evening.

item.title: Cross-border workers, M5S VCO asks for answers on NASpI and healthcare
item.description: After the September 17 meeting in Rome, M5S VCO calls for a binding timetable on the healthcare contribution, NASpI and tax option.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- The interministerial table met on September 17. - The next meeting is scheduled for November 9, 2026. - NASpI, health contributions, and tax options remain open issues. - M5S VCO is requesting a binding timetable.
- Table → second session on September 17 in Rome - Start → February 2025 - Next meeting → November 9, 2026, at the Ministry of Labour - Health contribution → introduced on January 1, 2024 - Trade unions → CGIL, CISL, and UIL
On September 17, in Rome, the second session of the interministerial table on cross-border work was limited, according to the Movimento 5 Stelle VCO, to confirming the operating procedures provided for by the regulations. This is the second step of a table established in February 2025 and tasked with defining a statute for cross-border workers.
The group returns to the topic following the press release of August 10, which had gathered the appeal of the unions at the Festa della Lucciola in Villadossola. The update stems from two events on the same day: the meeting in Rome and the statements made by Alberto Preioni, Undersecretary to the Presidency of the Piedmont Region, who attended the table representing the Region.
### The dossiers indicated by the unions
According to the Movement's reconstruction, the core issue is the failure to move to a substantive discussion. A year and a half after the start and months after the first meeting, workers are waiting for answers on issues that directly affect their income and rights. The CGIL, CISL, and UIL organizations reiterated this in a joint note signed by Giuseppe Augurusa, Marco Contessa, and Pancrazio Raimondo.
Among the requests is the implementing circular on the treatment of NASpI in the first months of payment, a topic linked to cross-border unemployment. The note also asks to safeguard the principle of non-double taxation regarding the health contribution introduced on January 1, 2024, which still lacks the implementing decree. Also mentioned are the full implementation of the tax option for trans-cantonal cross-border workers—the so-called 'omnibus decree', agreed with the Mef but not shared by the border Cantons; the study on extending conventional salaries to weekly cross-border workers; and the full application of the Single and Universal Allowance for incoming and outgoing cross-border workers.

item.description: VPOD-SSP rejects funding the 13th AVS pension payment through a VAT increase, popular vote on November 29; AVS profits of 5.6 billion in 2024 and 4.4 billion in 2025, assets of 60.4 billion.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - VPOD-SSP rejects financing through a VAT increase - The popular vote is scheduled for 29 novembre - The AVS has profits of over 10 billion in two years - The increase would cost 180 francs per family
## Key facts - Who: VPOD-SSP - What: financing the 13th AVS pension through a VAT increase - When: popular vote on 29 novembre - Where: delegates' assembly meeting in Zurich - Decision: 22 votes to 6 - AVS profits: 5,6 billion in 2024 and 4,4 billion in 2025 - Assets: 60,4 billion, equal to 113% of annual expenditure - Average cost: 180 francs more per year per family
On 26 settembre 2026, in Zurich, VPOD-SSP decided to recommend rejecting the financing of the 13th AVS pension through a VAT increase, which will be put to a popular vote on 29 novembre. The decision was taken by the delegates' assembly by 22 votes to 6, as reported in a statement issued today.
The trade union considers additional short-term financing unjustified. The reason given is the state of the AVS's finances, which VPOD-SSP describes as very solid. The organization therefore maintains that there is no sufficient reason to resort immediately to an increase in value-added tax.
### The figures cited by the trade union
In 2024, the AVS is said to have recorded profits of 5,6 billion francs, while profits in 2025 are said to have amounted to 4,4 billion. VPOD-SSP thus speaks of over 10 billion in two years. It adds a record asset base of 60,4 billion, equal to 113% of annual expenditure.
The trade union compares these amounts with the revenue expected from the VAT increase: 1,5 billion francs per year for six years. In its assessment, the profits accumulated over two years would exceed what the tax increase would yield during the period indicated.
The other criticism concerns the nature of VAT, which VPOD-SSP calls an antisocial and regressive tax. The increase would be the second in four years and would cost an average of 180 francs more per year per family. The trade union also argues that the measure would fuel inflation, add to increases in health-insurance premiums, and reduce purchasing power.
Finally, VPOD-SSP invokes the consistency of the trade-union position. During the campaign for the 13th AVS pension, it had been asserted that additional financing would not be necessary; for the long term, by contrast, an increase in wage contributions rather than in VAT had been advocated. For the trade union, raising the tax would represent a victory for employers. For a cross-border worker following the news from Canton Ticino, the first practical point coincides with the source's limitation: the text discusses the financing of the 13th AVS pension and the effect attributed to VAT, but does not address the G permit, withholding tax, LPP, LAMal, rebates, INPS, double taxation, Brogeda or the new 2026 tax agreement. The figure of 180 francs is presented as an annual average per family. It is not an individual deduction, it is not an amount relating to a payslip, and the source does not specifically attribute it to cross-border workers. A worker therefore cannot automatically turn that figure into a change in their monthly net pay. The point made by VPOD-SSP is the general effect on purchasing power, together with inflation and increases in health-insurance premiums.

If the proposal were not approved, the source does not describe what financing would take its place immediately. It only indicates the union's preference for an increase in wage contributions in the long term. item.description: Eugenio Zoffili questions Minister Schillaci and calls for technical working groups and exemptions to keep the Erba maternity unit operational.

## In brief - The maternity unit in Erba is scheduled to close - Eugenio Zoffili has submitted a parliamentary question - The request includes technical working groups and possible exemptions - The area mentioned includes Erbese, Vallassina and Triangolo Lariano
## Key facts - Facility → maternity unit of Erba Hospital - Main figure → Eugenio Zoffili - Addressee → Health Minister Schillaci - Party → Lega Salvini Premier - Area → Erbese, Vallassina and Triangolo Lariano - Parameter → 500 births per year - Requested solutions → technical working groups and exemption mechanisms
The forthcoming closure of the maternity unit at Erba Hospital has reached Parliament through a parliamentary question addressed to Health Minister Schillaci. It was submitted by Eugenio Zoffili, a deputy from Como and group leader of Lega Salvini Premier on Erba City Council. This position was taken after news of the forthcoming closure of the maternity unit, which Zoffili intends to oppose by asking that all solutions useful for keeping it operational be examined.
«The maternity unit at Erba Hospital must not be touched.» With these words, Zoffili reiterated that he had personally asked the owners several times to take a step back and to verify with Regione Lombardia whether an exemption was possible. The question to the minister stems from the same objective: to examine every useful solution to prevent the closure of the maternity unit.
### The two working groups requested by Zoffili
In the text of the question, the deputy specifically points to the opportunity to open a technical working group between the Government and the Region. This should be accompanied by a local working group involving all interested parties: mayors, administrators, trade unions and associations. Zoffili says he has already asked the Mayor for the latter, with the aim of concretely verifying the conditions needed to keep the maternity unit operational, including through the exemption mechanisms provided for by law.
The argument concerns a hospital that, according to the account provided, serves a large area: Erbese, Vallassina and Triangolo Lariano. In these areas, Zoffili argues, the proximity of healthcare services is also essential because of the area’s geographical characteristics. The parameter of 500 births per year is recognized as a factor to consider, but not as the only evaluation criterion. The same legislation, he adds, provides for the possibility of exemptions. Parliament has also already highlighted the need to identify solutions capable of guaranteeing safe healthcare services as close as possible to citizens. This is the point also raised in the in-depth analysis on servizi sanitari.
Lega, Zoffili concludes, will continue to work in Parliament and locally to defend the maternity unit and all related services. In his words, the mobilization should continue with the support of the local community, which is asking for opposition to what it calls an unacceptable decision. For a cross-border reader of the news, the practical connection must remain within the boundaries indicated by the source. The text discusses a healthcare facility serving a broad area and describes proximity as a value linked to geography. The matter therefore remains tied to the possible closure of the birth center and the search for a solution to prevent it.
For the cross-border reader, the news does not make it possible to calculate an individual impact. It does, however, make it possible to identify the criterion used in the comparison: distance and the configuration of the territory should be weighed together with the number of births and the safety of the services. The general overview of servizi sanitari may offer a separate reference, but it does not replace the contents of the parliamentary question.
### The situation before any possible outcome
| Element | What emerges from the source | |---|---| | Status of the matter | The closure is described as imminent and is being challenged | | Numerical assessment | 500 births per year to be considered, but not the only element | | Territorial assessment | The proximity of services matters because of the geographical characteristics | | Solutions indicated | Government-Region discussions, a territorial working group and exemptions |
This distinction avoids two opposite readings. On the one hand, the parameter of 500 births per year is not ignored: Zoffili states that it must be taken into consideration. On the other hand, the position expressed maintains that this figure cannot by itself conclude the assessment, because the area served is broad and the proximity of services is identified as a fundamental element.
The reference to the exemption must also be read precisely. The source recalls the possibility provided for by legislation and asks that its use be verified; it does not, however, present an exemption that has already been obtained. The same applies to the two working groups: they are instruments indicated in the parliamentary question and the territorial request, not an outcome that has already been reported. For those who live in the area described, the concrete issue is therefore the comparison between the numerical criterion, safety and the proximity of services.

Separate the institutional level from the local one: on the one hand, the technical working group between the Government and the Region, and on the other, the local working group. 3. Consider the parties already indicated: mayors, administrators, trade unions and associations. Zoffili reports having requested the local working group from the Mayor. 4. Assess maintaining operations using all the elements mentioned: 500 births per year, geographical characteristics, proximity and safety of services, as well as the exemption mechanisms.
### The questions to follow
To stay up to date on the situation, the reader can check whether the owners will reconsider the decision, whether the Government and the Region will open the technical working group, whether the local discussion will be organized and whether an exemption will be considered. item.title: Living in Merone and working in Ticino as a cross-border commuter
item.description: Living in Merone and working in Ticino: what changes regarding withholding tax, deductibles of 7.500 and 10.000 euro, AVS, LPP and LAMal.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Agreement signed on 23 dicembre 2020, in force from 1° gennaio 2024 - Old cross-border commuters: exemption of 7.500 euros until 2033 - New cross-border commuters: allowance of 10.000 euros - Employment tax withheld only in Switzerland
## Key facts - Cross-border commuters agreement → signed on 23 dicembre 2020; in force from 1° gennaio 2024 - Italian ratification → Law 83 of 13 giugno 2023 - Old cross-border commuters → exemption of 7.500 euros, transitional regime 2024–2033 - New cross-border commuters → allowance of 10.000 euros - Employment income → withholding tax only in Switzerland
The New Cross-Border Commuters Agreement between Italy and Switzerland was signed on 23 dicembre 2020. Italy ratified it with Law 83 of 13 giugno 2023, and the text entered into force on 1° gennaio 2024. For those who live in Merone and work in Canton Ticino as cross-border commuters, these dates define the framework to be checked before considering a move.
### The dates that separate the two regimes
The stated dividing date is 17 luglio 2023. Anyone who was already a cross-border commuter before that date falls into the category of old cross-border commuters: they benefit from the exemption of 7.500 euros and the transitional regime from 2024 to 2033. New cross-border commuters, on the other hand, have an allowance of 10.000 euros. The first check therefore concerns one’s status on the established date, not only the place of residence or the commute to work.
Regarding employment income, the stated rule is clear: for cross-border commuters, withholding tax is withheld only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit reported in section CE of form 730. This concerns the tax return and can be explored in greater detail in dichiarazione dei redditi, without turning the credit into a second taxation of the same income.
The Italy–Switzerland Convention for the avoidance of double taxation was signed on 9 marzo 1976. Switzerland is not a member of the EU or the EEA: this reference should be kept distinct from the agreement that entered into force in 2024.
Swiss tax rates, including federal and cantonal rates, are established by federal and cantonal laws. At federal level, administration falls under AFC/ESTV, while the cantonal tax administrations are also involved. For the reader from Merone, the review therefore begins with classifying the regime and reading the Swiss payslip together with the Italian tax section. translated text Before deciding whether to move from Merone and work in Ticino, it is worth turning the rules into a personal worksheet. The aim is not to estimate a generic amount, but to arrive at an orderly review of tax regime, payslip, healthcare and tax return.
### Five practical steps
1. Set the reference date. Write down whether you were already a cross-border worker before 17 luglio 2023. This information determines the group to compare: old cross-border workers with an exemption of 7.500 euro and transitional period 2024-2033, or new cross-border workers with an allowance of 10.000 euro.
2. Note the main tax rule. The cross-border worker's employment income is subject to withholding tax only in Switzerland. In the file, keep the reference to the tax credit in the CE section of the 730, which serves to avoid double taxation in Italy. For the tax-return section, use the dichiarazione dei redditi as a checkpoint.
3. Read the payslip by blocks. Identify AVS/AI/IPG at 5,3%, AD/AC at 1,1% with a cap of CHF 148'200, LAINF between 0,7% and 1,5%, and LPP between 7% and 18% according to the age bracket starting from the 25esimo year. The method prevents confusing contributions, insurance and withholding tax.
4. Check the healthcare position. With the G permit, there is an option right for LAMal. Note the reference adult deductible, ranging between CHF 300 and CHF 2'500, and keep it separate from social-security deductions. item.title: Protest in Castiglione d'Intelvi over concrete batching plant
item.description: Over 750 signatures collected in six days against the concrete batching plant and crusher planned in Castiglione d'Intelvi for the Tremezzina Bypass.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - More than 750 signatures collected in six days - Plant and crusher planned in Castiglione d’Intelvi - The protest concerns the location, not the Bypass - Concerns about dust, noise, water and heavy traffic
## Key facts - Project → concrete batching plant with crusher - Location → municipal territory of Castiglione d’Intelvi - Signature collection → more than 750 signatures in six days - Stated duration → six years - Nearby areas → schools, nursing homes and the Oratory of the Madonna del Restello - Portal → intelviradar.it
More than 750 signatures in six days: the mobilization against the proposal for a concrete batching plant in Castiglione d’Intelvi has reached a significant initial threshold. The project also includes a crusher intended to process stones from the excavations. The area identified is populated and not far from schools, nursing homes and places of cultural interest, including the Oratory of the Madonna del Restello.
The Intelvi Valley has thus returned to the center of news coverage because of operations linked to the construction site of the Tremezzina Bypass. After the Cava Citrini affair, which ended positively for residents, attention has shifted to a second plant proposal. A longtime source for the newspaper, whose identifying details are known but who is not identified, describes a protest that has now erupted.
> «An uproar is breaking out in the Intelvi Valley, people have finally realized what a concrete batching plant is! Especially because of the six-year duration specified in the project, noise and environmental pollution, and traffic that will bring the valley to its knees».
The same source recalls that residents had managed to get the first proposed location at Cava Citrini abandoned. After years without any action, it adds, an area at the entrance to Castiglione would now be in preparation. This reference links the new mobilization to the previous protest, shifting attention to the second proposal.
### From concrete production to the crusher
The concrete batching plant is described as an industrial system for storing, measuring out and precisely mixing the ingredients of fresh concrete. Alongside it, the crusher would process the excavated stones. For the proponents, the duration specified in the project, six years, makes the choice of location decisive.
### The protest and its scope
The document circulated by residents specifies that the mobilization is not against the Tremezzina Bypass. The opposition concerns the plant’s location and the anticipated consequences for health, the environment, road traffic, safety and the valley’s tourism and residential character. The concerns include dust and noise, water consumption, possible effects on soil and groundwater, as well as the passage of heavy vehicles carrying stones, concrete and water from the lake. ## How to follow the mobilization
The operational guidelines contained in the document focus on information, participation and institutional dialogue. The channel indicated by citizens is the intelviradar.it portal, activated to ensure transparency, regular updates and access to information about the project and the initiatives.
### From the portal to the assembly
1. Consult intelviradar.it for updates on the project and the mobilization. 2. Learn more on the portal about the reasons for the protest and the issues contested by citizens. 3. Look for information on how to sign the petition promoted by the community. 4. Follow the request for a public assembly with Mario Pozzi, identified as the Mayor of the municipality most affected, and with all representatives of the institutions involved.
The only timeline reported in the source concerns the collection of signatures: more than 750 signatures were reached in six days. This figure measures the speed of the mobilization, but is not presented as a deadline for signing. The document does not indicate a date for the assembly, a deadline for the petition or a work schedule.
To avoid misunderstandings, the organizers’ request should be kept distinct from the main project. The text specifies that the protest does not concern the Variante della Tremezzina, but rather the location of the facility and its possible consequences. Those consulting the portal can therefore focus on the concrete batching plant, the related crusher, the road network and the requests addressed to the administrations.
Citizens are asking institutions and the competent administrations, starting with the Municipalities of the Valley, for greater transparency toward the population and a review of the project. The request is justified by the protection of the environment, public health and the future of Val d’Intelvi. The source records this request for dialogue, without reporting the outcome of an assembly or a review.

item.title: Robbery at Bennet: alleged mastermind arrested in Ticino
item.description: A 32-year-old resident of the Bellinzona area and a 25-year-old from Monza were arrested for the robbery at the Stroili jewelry store in the Bennet shopping center in Tavernola.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - A 32-year-old resident of the Bellinzona area arrested - A 25-year-old resident in the province of Monza also arrested - Stroili jewelry store at Bennet in Tavernola targeted - Loot estimated at around 90'000 euro
## Key facts - Arrests: Friday 25 settembre - Investigation: Como State Police - Robbery: 24 aprile - Location: Bennet in Tavernola, Como - Detention: Bassone prison
### The arrest in Como On Friday 25 settembre, the Como State Police arrested a 32-year-old Italian man residing in the Bellinzona area as part of the investigation into the armed robbery at the Stroili jewelry store in the Bennet shopping center in Tavernola, Como. According to initial reconstructions, the man was allegedly the mastermind of the criminal group.
In the same operation, a 25-year-old resident of the province of Monza was arrested. The two measures were carried out on the basis of a pre-trial detention order issued by the judge for preliminary investigations in Como at the request of the Public Prosecutor's Office. Both were transferred to the Como prison, the Bassone prison.
The robbery for which the investigation was launched dates back to 24 aprile. Four people, all disguised, had reached the jewelry store in a rental car. One of the members had remained at the wheel, while the other three had entered the shop with their faces covered by balaclavas.
The three who entered the jewelry store were armed with a pistol and had hammers. After threatening the employees with the weapon, they had smashed the glass display cases and taken possession of numerous gold jewelry items. The total value of the goods had been estimated at around 90'000 euro.
The last two arrests came after those of the other three members of the group, carried out by the Como Mobile Squad between April and May. According to the investigation, the case thus involves all the alleged participants in the raid that took place in the Tavernola shopping center. ## The reconstruction of the heist
The robbery at the Stroili jewelry store in Bennet in Tavernola had been prepared using a rental car. Four people were inside, all disguised. One had remained at the wheel; the other three had reached the store to carry out the heist.
Inside the jewelry store, the three had their faces covered by balaclavas and had entered with a pistol and hammers. The employees had been threatened with the weapon. The hammers had been used to smash the glass display cases, from which numerous gold jewelry items had been taken.
The operation had unfolded in a few minutes. Before fleeing, the people who had entered the store had managed to take jewelry with a total estimated value of around 90'000 euros. The robbery had been described as particularly violent and similar to a scene from a Hollywood action film.
### The arrests and the stolen goods
The investigations by the Como Mobile Squad had led to the arrest of the other three members of the group between April and May. Subsequent inquiries had enabled investigators to reconstruct, according to the prosecution, the roles of the various participants.
Investigators had also gathered evidence against the alleged mastermind. During searches carried out after the arrests, part of the stolen goods had been recovered before they could enter the channels for handling stolen goods.
The recovered jewelry had subsequently been returned to the jewelry store. The recovery was one of the developments in the investigation into the robbery of 24 April, together with the evidence collected by the Mobile Squad to reconstruct the roles of the people involved, according to the prosecution. ## The continuation of the investigation
With the arrests carried out on Friday 25 September, the investigation into the 24 April robbery now involves all the alleged participants in the heist. The latest measure concerns the 32-year-old Italian resident in the Bellinzonese area and the 25-year-old resident in the province of Monza, while the other three arrests had already been carried out between April and May.
The two men arrested on Friday were remanded in custody at the Como prison, Bassone. The order was issued by the investigating judge in Como at the request of the Public Prosecutor’s Office. The arrest therefore represents the latest development reported in the investigation by the Como State Police.
### Responsibility still to be established The source specifies that the responsibility of the two arrested men, as well as that of the other suspects, will have to be established during the subsequent stages of the proceedings. This also concerns the role attributed to the 32-year-old: according to initial reconstructions, the man was allegedly the mastermind of the criminal group.
The investigations enabled investigators to reconstruct, according to the prosecution, the roles of the various participants and to gather evidence also against the alleged instigator. These are the elements on which the proceedings will continue after the two men’s transfer to Bassone prison.
The developments already reported also include searches carried out following the arrests and the recovery of part of the stolen goods. The jewelry had been returned to the jewelry store before it could enter the channels for handling stolen goods. The assessment of responsibility remains entrusted to the subsequent stages of the proceedings, as specified for all the suspects.

On 12 and 13 September, LIUC – Università Cattaneo represented Italy in the first edition of Industrial Quest, the initiative promoted by ERIH – European Route of Industrial Heritage. Italian participation focused on Cotonificio Cantoni, with a route dedicated to traces of its history still visible on the university campus in Castellanza.
The initiative concluded after two days designed to bring the public closer to Europe’s industrial heritage through a participatory and itinerant format. At the various venues, museums, historic production sites and places of industrial memory offered activities to be completed with a smartphone: quizzes, observation exercises, estimation questions, searches for details of buildings and photographic challenges.

The stated objective was to transform the visit into an active exploration experience. ## In brief - On-board ticket: 3,20 euro in the attached receipt - Card not working, according to the student - From 23 settembre, access, traffic flow and parking change - Insubria indicates lines C, E and reinforcement services

The on-board ticket purchased on a bus heading to the Bizzozero university campus cost 3,20 euro according to the receipt attached to the report. The amount is double the normal fare indicated by the student.
The student at Università dell'Insubria wrote to VareseNews. She and some classmates had not bought the ticket in advance and were not subscribers: they thought they could purchase it on board.
On board, however, the card payment device was not working, according to her account. “It was therefore only possible to buy the ticket with coins,” the student recounts. The driver issued the tickets, applying the surcharge provided for those who had not purchased them beforehand and did not have a pass.
### The fare applied
The surcharge for purchasing on board is provided for by the service rules. Therefore, formally speaking, the driver's behavior is not an anomaly. The letter instead raises a question about occasional access: how easy is it to use the bus in Varese without being regular users?
In the reported case, it was possible to buy the ticket on board, but card payment was not available on the service in question, leaving coins as the only option. The receipt made the effect of the surcharge visible: 3,20 euro.

The report comes as the Bizzozero Campus changes its access, traffic flow and parking arrangements. From 23 settembre, new arrangements linked to work for new parking areas and, later, a multifunctional building came into force.
Università dell'Insubria invited students and staff, whenever possible, to favor public transport. It points to urban lines C and E and the additional services of the university reinforcement service as alternatives to the car.
The university is also continuing the Bus Insubria service between central Varese and Bizzozero, carpooling, and agreements for shared bicycles and scooters. The initiatives dedicated to university mobility focus on the Varese Campus and the need to reduce the number of cars heading to the campus every day. ## The point for those who use the service occasionally
The report separates two aspects that often end up in the same incident. On the one hand, there is a fare rule: a ticket bought on board entails a surcharge.
